responsivePlay.landscape: Board left; compact status right; current score stays visible; orientation never starts a new run.
responsivePlay.boardSizingSource: src/layout.js measures actual status, actions, captions, safe-area padding and visible viewport; sets --board-size.
responsivePlay.compactControls: Minimum 44px common-control height at widths up to 1100px or with a coarse pointer.
responsivePlay.compactContent: Hide secondary piece legend and repeated captions; preserve goals, moves, current score, three-star score and actions.
responsivePlay.touchSource: src/input.js uses dominant-direction swipes, tremor tolerance, adjacent-cell bounds, pointer cancellation and primary-pointer ownership.
responsivePlay.effectResize: Rebase active-frame geometry while retaining elapsed animation time and paused state.
responsivePlay.evidence: docs/RESPONSIVE_TEST_REPORT.md and docs/testing/; actual browser viewport checks, not physical iOS or Android certification.

narrative.overview:
The page theme is a quiet night outside a lit workshop: navy backgrounds, cool blue surfaces, soft pale text, and honey-gold primary actions. The original color and background refinement preserved the page and board layouts. A later explicit user request replaced the five glass-piece illustrations with round cartoon cat, rabbit, fox, penguin and bear faces. No generated imagery is used.

`night.css` is the normative page-theme layer; `styles.css` owns layout, board and animations. `src/pieces.js` is the canonical source for authored inline animal SVGs, Chinese names and animal palettes. The workshop's glass windows and story remain part of the setting.
keyCharacteristics: Round animal faces distinct by silhouette, features and color

rules.name: The Board Boundary Rule
rules.body: Page-theme rules in `night.css` must not override board, piece, obstacle or effect selectors. The explicit animal replacement belongs to the piece source and its narrow styling.

rules.name: The Text Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Use warm off-white headings, blue-tinted utility text, and gold actions and score.

dos: Do keep the foreground readable on every surface, including settings and chapter tabs.
Do use CSS for the page background and local authored vector artwork.
Do keep animal silhouettes, facial features and special direction/type marks distinct at small piece sizes.
Do keep the shared animal definitions and stable saved piece keys aligned across artwork, goals, legend, tutorial, accessibility labels and effect light colors.
Do keep motion preferences, focus behavior, target information and responsive play intact.
donts: Don't introduce generated illustrations, raster mockups, remote assets or decorative English headings.

Don't restyle the board, replace its pieces, rewrite gameplay or rearrange page layouts as part of a palette-only theme change. The later explicit animal-piece request authorizes the documented artwork replacement within its narrow scope.
Don't apply broad SVG recoloring that overrides the animal faces or hides their special markers.
